result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_multi_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Count multi-edges (parallel edges between same node pair). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4858-L4893){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_multi_edges() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Only counts edges beyond the first one for each node pair. For example, if there are 3 edges from `A` to `B`, this counts 2 of them. Multi-edges are useful for modeling scenarios like multiple flights between cities or repeated transactions. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of duplicate edges (beyond first edge per pair). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Count multi-edges in a directed graph: ::: {#bbdc7539 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge("A", "B", id=1) .add_edge("A", "B", id=2) # Multi-edge .add_edge("A", "B", id=3) # Another multi-edge .add_edge("B", "A", id=4) # Different direction ) # Returns 2 graph.count_multi_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
